target_stage: Delhi High Court CM(M) petition challenging concurrent ARC and Rent Control Tribunal rejection of the subletting ground

IK-33810117:L61:span1.text: the premises described as third floor of property bearing No.4-E/7, Jhandewalan Extension, New Delhi (subject premises), let out initially by a lease deed (Ex.PW-1/R1) dated 27. 06.1979 in the name of a partnership firm described as M/s. Current Advertising and Marketing in which M.L. Aggarwal and R.P. Aggarwal were partners.

IK-33810117:L62:span2.text: It is further an admitted fact that the said partnership firm was converted into a private limited company in the name and style of M/s. Current Advertising (P) Limited (the first respondent)

IK-33810117:L63:span3.text: It is further undisputed that the tenancy rights were transferred in the name of the first respondent, it having been accepted as the tenancy qua the subject premises with effect from 27.03.1990.

IK-33810117:L63:span4.text: It is admitted that the said Directors of the first respondent company parted ways w.e.f April, 1992 where after one of them, viz., M.L. Aggarwal took over the said company, having shifted elsewhere, the other Director (R.P. Aggarwal) continuing on the subject premises retaining its control.

IK-33810117:L64:span5.text: The subject premises concededly came to be in use and occupation of M/s. Censor Advertising Pvt. Ltd., (second respondent), a company in which R.P. Aggarwal is a Director.

IK-33810117:L65:span6.text: the first respondent (the tenant) had sub- let the subject premises to the second respondent without the previous consent in writing of the landlord

IK-33810117:L67:span7.text: The trial court, however, was of the view that the petitioners had failed to prove the CM(M) 433/2013 Page 2 of 5 ground of subletting and, thus, dismissed the petition on that ground.

IK-33810117:L68:span8.text: the said having been dismissed by the judgment dated 15.12.2012.
